title: Tenali Raman Tale 90

full_text:
A vain and wealthy textile merchant named Shreshthi Manikchand was obsessed with appearances. He wore fine silks, perfumed his mustache with musk, and bragged that everything he owned was of pure gold or celestial quality.
One afternoon, during a public gathering at the town square, Manikchand pointed to a passing washerman’s grey donkey and sneered:
'Look at that wretched beast! Common folk surround themselves with coarse, ugly animals. If I owned a donkey, I would wash its tail with rosewater and imported silk soap every morning until the hair turned into pure, shining golden silk!'

The crowd laughed at his arrogant boasting.
Tenali Raman, who was standing nearby, resolved to test the merchant's claim.

The next morning, Tenali arrived outside Manikchand’s grand mansion leading an old, patient grey donkey.
Tenali tied the donkey to the merchant's front gatepost, pulled up a wooden stool, brought out a copper bowl of warm water, a bar of soap, and began scrubbing the donkey's coarse tail with immense, theatrical concentration!

A large crowd gathered to watch.
Tenali lathered the donkey’s tail with soap, rinsed it, combed the coarse hairs, and repeated the process:
Lather, rinse, scrub, comb!
The donkey occasionally swished its wet tail, splattering soapy water across Tenali’s face and clothes!

Merchant Manikchand stepped out of his mansion, frowning in annoyance:
'Tenali! Why art thou washing that dirty donkey’s tail at my front gate, blocking my customers?'

Tenali looked up with earnest sincerity:
'Shreshthi-ji! I am putting your brilliant doctrine into practice!
You proclaimed yesterday that by washing a donkey's tail with soap and devotion, the coarse hair would turn into pure, shining golden silk!
I have been scrubbing for three hours, and I am waiting for the gold to appear!'

Manikchand stammered, his face reddening:
'Tenali, art thou a fool? No matter how much soap thou usest, a donkey’s tail is made of coarse hair; it will never turn into silk!'

Tenali stood up, wiped the soap foam from his eyes, and addressed the laughing crowd:
'Hear the wise merchant’s confession!
A donkey’s tail remains a donkey’s tail, no matter how much rosewater and soap thou washest it with!
And an arrogant man remains a hollow boaster, no matter how many fine silk robes he wears to disguise his empty mind!'

The entire crowd roared with laughter, clapping and cheering.
Manikchand retreated into his mansion in utter disgrace, cured of his boastful vanity, while Tenali untied the donkey and returned it to the washerman with a basket of fresh greens.
moral: Pretentious vanity that seeks to transform basic reality into false luxury makes itself an object of ridicule.
